name: What is the difference between office build-out, tenant improvement, and office fit-out?

mainEntity.name: Are office build-out, tenant improvement, and fit-out the same thing, or do they mean different scopes?
mainEntity.text: Are office build-out, tenant improvement, and fit-out the same thing, or do they mean different scopes?

acceptedAnswer.text: In practice, office build-out, tenant improvement, and fit-out are closely related terms, but the emphasis can differ. Build-out usually refers to the construction work required to turn a shell or former tenant space into a functional office. Tenant improvement often describes the lease and funding side of that same work, especially when discussing TI allowances, landlord contributions, or tenant-paid upgrades. Fit-out is commonly used to describe the overall process of designing and finishing the interior. The important issue is not the label but the scope. A project in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, or North Hollywood should clearly define what is included: demolition, framing, glass offices, conference rooms, break areas, lighting, HVAC changes, data cabling, restrooms, and finishes. Clear scope language prevents budget disputes and change orders later.
acceptedAnswer.description: These terms are often used interchangeably, but they can imply slightly different things. An office build-out usually means constructing the interior improvements needed to make a leased space usable, while tenant improvement refers to the broader leasehold work funded or shared by the landlord and tenant. Fit-out often describes the same process from a design and construction perspective.
